overview: Senegal is a country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa. Its capital and largest city, Dakar, stands on the Cap-Vert peninsula, the westernmost point of mainland Africa. Senegal became independent from France in 1960 and has a long tradition of peaceful democracy. Gorée Island, off Dakar, is a memorial to the Atlantic slave trade.

geography.text: Senegal is mostly low and flat, with savanna in the centre and south and dry Sahel in the north. The Senegal river forms its northern border, and Senegal almost completely surrounds the Gambia. Near Dakar, Lac Rose is a salt lake whose water can turn pink.

history.text: The region was part of the Ghana, Mali and Jolof empires. Gorée Island became a slave-trading post, and France gradually took control in the 1800s, making Dakar the capital of French West Africa. Senegal became independent in 1960 under the poet Léopold Sédar Senghor and has never had a military coup.

events.title: Dakar capital
events.text: Dakar becomes capital of French West Africa.

events.title: Peaceful change
events.text: Power passes peacefully to an opposition leader.
